sentences.en: And if you don't say yes immediately and we don't see you, you don't have a job at General Motors anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果你不立即答应，我们又看不到你，你在通用汽车就再也没有工作了。

sentences.en: This isn't even signed by anybody.
sentences.zh: 这甚至连个签名都没有。

sentences.en: You know, you send 100 of these out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们发出了100封这样的信。

sentences.en: 10 years for a company and that's what you get.
sentences.zh: 为一家公司干了10年，结果就得到这个。

sentences.en: That sounds horrible.
sentences.zh: 听起来太糟糕了。

sentences.en: He's thinking, okay, I have this house we built.
sentences.zh: 他在想，好吧，我们建了这栋房子。

sentences.en: My daughter has this school.
sentences.zh: 我女儿在这上学。

sentences.en: My wife works in the health care industry here.
sentences.zh: 我妻子就在这里的医疗行业工作。

sentences.en: I don't want to move.
sentences.zh: 我不想搬家。

sentences.en: And I don't even know if I can.
sentences.zh: 而且我甚至不知道自己能不能搬。

sentences.en: And I certainly can't in 10 days' time.
sentences.zh: 我肯定没办法在10天之内搬走。

sentences.en: Now you've got to figure something else out.
sentences.zh: 现在你必须想点别的办法了。

sentences.en: What's your next plan?
sentences.zh: 你的下一步计划是什么？

sentences.en: Because now your health care, your vision, your dental, all of it's gone.
sentences.zh: 因为现在你的医疗保险、视力保险、牙科保险，全都没了。

sentences.en: Because I don't want to pick up and go 700 miles.
sentences.zh: 因为我不想背井离乡搬去700英里外。

sentences.en: You know, it's not even fair.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这甚至都不公平。

sentences.en: How is this considered an option?
sentences.zh: 这怎么能算是一个选择呢？

sentences.en: So he doesn't go.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有去。

sentences.en: What about your original question about the ramifications of all of this, politically, for President Trump?
sentences.zh: 那你最初关于这一切在政治上对特朗普总统产生的影响的问题呢？

sentences.en: So Brant's reaction was, I thought, pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为布兰特的反应相当有趣。

sentences.en: Do you feel like he's part of this at all or no?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他卷入了这件事吗，还是完全没有？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 完全没有。

sentences.en: This is, it kind of annoys me when people think that, you know, he's part of them closing this.
sentences.zh: 每当人们认为，你知道的，他是他们关闭工厂的幕后推手时，这有点让我恼火。

sentences.en: And this is a company decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个公司做出的决定。

sentences.en: You've got to put blame where it's due.
sentences.zh: 该怪谁就得怪谁。

sentences.en: He said it's about a company and what it's deciding to do.
sentences.zh: 他说这关乎一家公司以及它决定要做的事。

sentences.en: And I'm really angry at this company.
sentences.zh: 我对这家公司感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's funny.
sentences.zh: 对，这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: I see all these signs with Trump's face on it about how bad things are here in Lordstown.
sentences.zh: 我看到所有这些印有特朗普头像的标语，上面写着洛兹敦的现状有多糟。

sentences.en: Well, where's the signs with Mary's face on it?
sentences.zh: 那么，印有玛丽头像的标语在哪里呢？

sentences.en: This is her company.
sentences.zh: 这是她的公司。

sentences.en: Trump don't sign my paycheck.
sentences.zh: 特朗普可不给我发工资。

sentences.en: Trump didn't send me this letter.
sentences.zh: 特朗普也没有给我发这封信。

sentences.en: There's nothing on here about Trump Industries or anything.
sentences.zh: 上面什么也没有提到特朗普工业或别的什么。

sentences.en: It says GM, General Motors.
sentences.zh: 上面写的是通用汽车，即General Motors。

sentences.en: I know this reaction very well from my own reporting.
sentences.zh: 我从自己的报道中对这种反应再熟悉不过了。

sentences.en: People feel like when you ask them about the political ramifications of something like their plant closing, their response is often, you know,
sentences.zh: 人们觉得，当你问及他们工厂倒闭之类事情的政治影响时，他们的回应往往是，你知道的，

sentences.en: you're whittling down my experience of loss to this one thing that's important to you.
sentences.zh: 你把我的失落经历缩小成了对你而言重要的一件小事。

sentences.en: But that's not necessarily what's important to me.
sentences.zh: 但那不一定是我所在乎的。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That was exactly what he was saying.
sentences.zh: 这正是他想表达的。

sentences.en: He was like, look, this is a huge problem for this community.
sentences.zh: 他当时的意思是，听着，这对这个社区来说是个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: This is a huge issue for my life.
sentences.zh: 这对我的生活来说是个极其严重的问题。

sentences.en: And, like, all you want to do is come here and, like, ask me about Trump.
sentences.zh: 而你们唯一想做的事，就是跑到这里来，向我打听特朗普。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in fact, when I talked to Dave Green, he's the head of the auto workers union in Lordstown.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我与戴夫·格林交谈时——他是洛兹敦汽车工人联合会的负责人，

sentences.en: He really spotted this right away.
sentences.zh: 他一下子就看穿了这一点。

sentences.en: He was like, oh, reporter lady, New York.
sentences.zh: 他当时就像是在说，哦，来自纽约的女记者啊。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: You want to ask me about Trump?
sentences.zh: 你想问我关于特朗普的事？

sentences.en: Oh, Trump.
sentences.zh: 哦，特朗普。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: I still like Trump?
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢特朗普吗？

sentences.en: Do I not like Trump anymore?
sentences.zh: 难道我不再喜欢特朗普了吗？

sentences.en: What is it about Trump?
sentences.zh: 特朗普到底怎么了？

sentences.en: He was hilarious.
sentences.zh: 他当时太搞笑了。

sentences.en: But I was like, oh, man.
sentences.zh: 但我当时想，天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, he has my number.
sentences.zh: 哦，他把我看透了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He saw you coming.
sentences.zh: 他早就料到你会来。

sentences.en: But did you get him to answer the question?
sentences.zh: 但你有没有让他正面回答这个问题？

sentences.en: I think a big piece of it is, you know, elections have consequences.
sentences.zh: 我认为很大一部分原因在于，你知道的，选举是有后果的。

sentences.en: So, Dave, you know, he is a Democratic voter and he was a Democratic voter in 2016.
sentences.zh: 所以，戴夫，你知道，他是一名民主党选民，在2016年他也是一名民主党选民。

sentences.en: And he gets why people voted for Trump.
sentences.zh: 他理解为什么人们会投票给特朗普。

sentences.en: He doesn't like it, but he gets it.
sentences.zh: 他虽然不喜欢，但他理解。

sentences.en: People continue to elect politicians that are not going to do the right thing by people.
sentences.zh: 人们不断选出那些无法为民众做正确之事的政客。

sentences.en: People are going to continue to suffer.
sentences.zh: 人们也将继续饱受苦难。

sentences.en: But he also was in a lot of ways really frustrated because he started in a country,
sentences.zh: 但在很多方面，他也感到非常沮丧，因为他最初生活在一个国家、

sentences.en: in a state that had a strong union and where people who were workers understood that it was through that union and through politics that they get a good deal for themselves and that that's the way it used to be.
sentences.zh: 一个拥有强大工会的州，那里的工人们明白，正是通过工会和政治，他们才能为自己争取到优厚的待遇，而且过去一直都是这样的。

sentences.en: You know, Walter Ruther, one of the big founders of this organization, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，沃尔特·鲁瑟，这个组织伟大的创始人们之一，对吧？

sentences.en: The ballot box is connected to the bread box.
sentences.zh: 选票箱与面包箱息息相关。

sentences.en: He preached that.
sentences.zh: 他一直这样宣讲。

sentences.en: And I think people understood that, that the politicians that we elect are going to give people either the opportunity to earn a good living or not.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们都懂这一点，我们选出的政客要么会给人们带来体面谋生的机会，要么就不会。

sentences.en: They're going to put money in the pockets of corporate America or the pockets of working America.
sentences.zh: 他们要么把钱塞进美国企业界的口袋，要么塞进美国工薪阶层的口袋。

sentences.en: So you better elect the right people because it's going to have a huge consequence on your livelihood.
sentences.zh: 所以你最好选对人，因为这会对你的生计产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: But, you know, Dave says things have really changed.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，戴夫说情况真的变了。

sentences.en: That's not the case anymore.
sentences.zh: 事实已经不再是那样了。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to get people to see the connection between politics and their lives, to understand that their votes have consequences,
sentences.zh: 而且要让人看到政治与他们生活之间的联系、让他们明白自己的选票是有后果的，这真的很难，

sentences.en: that they can hold politicians accountable.
sentences.zh: 让他们明白他们是可以追究政客责任的。

sentences.en: And that if they do, these things they're so sick of in their lives, they could actually change.
sentences.zh: 如果他们这么做了，生活中那些令他们深恶痛绝的事情，其实是可以改变的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你就可以。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 整整一个月，带你突破付费墙，体验《时报》订阅用户每天都能看到的内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》App，即可获得30天免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Sabrina, what explains that rift for people where they're not feeling a connection between their plant closing and the politicians they put in power?
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，人们为什么会出现这种割裂感，感受不到工厂倒闭与他们推选上台的政客之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: So I think in order to understand it, you have to go back as early as the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得要想理解这一点，你必须追溯到上世纪70年代。

sentences.en: This is the Campbell, Ohio steel mill of the Youngstown sheet and tube company.
sentences.zh: 这是扬斯敦钢管公司的坎贝尔俄亥俄钢铁厂。

sentences.en: This was a big manufacturing area in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，这是一个重要的制造业地区。

sentences.en: There were a huge number of steel plants.
sentences.zh: 当时有大量的钢铁厂。

sentences.en: Many of the steel workers at the Campbell Works are third-generation employees.
sentences.zh: 坎贝尔工厂的许多钢铁工人都是第三代员工。

sentences.en: And a lot of very good-paying jobs.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多薪酬非常优厚的工作。

sentences.en: But what started to happen for various reasons, including economic change, globalization, was that these plants started to close.
sentences.zh: 但由于经济变革、全球化等各种原因，这些工厂开始走向倒闭。

sentences.en: And there was a very famous closure in September of 1977 in Lordstown.
sentences.zh: 1977年9月，洛兹敦发生了一起非常著名的倒闭事件。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, the news we've received this morning from Youngstown sheet and tube is just the worst possible news.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，我们今天早上从扬斯敦钢管公司收到的消息绝对是最糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: About 10,000 people lost their jobs.
sentences.zh: 大约1万名工人失去了工作。

sentences.en: They have a name for the day disaster struck.
sentences.zh: 对于灾难降临的那一天，他们起了一个名字。

sentences.en: They call it Black Monday.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为黑色星期一。

sentences.en: Everybody remembers it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都记得。

sentences.en: Everybody.
sentences.zh: 所有人。

sentences.en: Working here for so many years, it's hard to believe that we're put out on the street and don't know what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 在这里工作了这么多年，真不敢相信我们就这样被赶到了街上，还不知道接下来该怎么办。

sentences.en: I put in 34 good years and I could be proud of mine for 34 years.
sentences.zh: 我付出了34年的好年华，我可以为我的这34年感到骄傲。

sentences.en: But that was the saddest moment I ever had when I came home.
sentences.zh: 但当我回到家时，那是我经历过最悲伤的时刻。

sentences.en: Where are politicians in all of this?
sentences.zh: 在这当中政客们都在干什么？

sentences.en: It was very much in those days the time of the Democratic Party and labor being absolutely hand-in-hand, glove-in-glove.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，民主党和工会的关系可以说是密不可分、形影不离。

sentences.en: So the Democratic politicians would be fighting these closures.
sentences.zh: 因此，民主党政客们会极力反对这些工厂倒闭。

sentences.en: And they would really be seen by workers in many ways as the guys who had their back.
sentences.zh: 而且在很多方面，工人们真的会把他们视作坚强后盾。

sentences.en: Carter eventually named a special task force which came up with some recommendations to help the steel industry as a whole.
sentences.zh: 卡特最终任命了一个特别工作组，提出了一些旨在帮助整个钢铁行业的建议。

sentences.en: The Democratic Party was the party of workers in the United States and that's who those workers were voting for.
sentences.zh: 民主党曾是美国工人们的党派，那些工人们投票支持的也正是他们。

sentences.en: But in the 1990s, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但在上世纪90年代，美国

sentences.en: government starts to have negotiations over a trade agreement known as NAFTA with Mexico and Canada to lower trade barriers so that it's easier for companies to do business across those lines.
sentences.zh: 政府开始就一项名为北美自由贸易协定（NAFTA）的贸易协议与墨西哥和加拿大展开谈判，旨在降低贸易壁垒，以便公司跨国开展业务更加容易。

sentences.en: It started by Republicans, but it's really finished in a big, splashy way by the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 这项协议由共和党人发起，但最终却由民主党以一种轰轰烈烈的方式大肆完成。

sentences.en: When I affix my signature to the NAFTA legislation a few moments from now, I do so with this pledge to the men and women of our country who were afraid of these changes.
sentences.zh: 稍后当我把名字签在北美自由贸易协定立法上时，我是带着这样一份承诺面向我们国家那些对这些变化感到恐惧的男女同胞们签下它的。

sentences.en: Bill Clinton is the one that signs on the dotted line at the end in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿就是在上世纪90年代最终在虚线下方签字的那个人。

sentences.en: The gains from this agreement will be your gains too.
sentences.zh: 这项协议带来的收益也将是你们的收益。

sentences.en: And at first, workers I talked to in Lordstown, they didn't really understand the implications of that.
sentences.zh: 起初，我在洛兹敦交流过的工人们并没有真正理解其中的含义。

sentences.en: But as the 1990s wore on and then into the early 2000s, things actually started to change.
sentences.zh: 但随着90年代的推移，直到2000年代初，情况真的开始发生变化了。

sentences.en: Supply chains started springing up in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 供应链开始在墨西哥涌现。

sentences.en: There was a lot of outsourcing that started to happen.
sentences.zh: 大量的外包业务开始出现。

sentences.en: Automation was happening as well.
sentences.zh: 自动化也在发生。

sentences.en: Technology was changing manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 科技正在改变制造业。

sentences.en: So many things were going on and people started to notice that the jobs were disappearing.
sentences.zh: 各种事情接踵而至，人们开始注意到工作岗位正在消失。

sentences.en: One worker I talked to, he started in the paint shop in the mid-1990s and it started with 38 workers.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一位工人，他于90年代中期进入涂装车间，当时车间有38名工人。

sentences.en: And when he left the paint shop in the early 2000s, there were only four.
sentences.zh: 而当他在2000年代初离开涂装车间时，只剩下4个人了。

sentences.en: So he described it as this almost kind of invisible hand kind of erasing things behind him as he went.
sentences.zh: 所以他将这形容为几乎像是有一只无形的手在他在场时把身后的东西统统抹去一样。

sentences.en: It could be coming for any of us.
sentences.zh: 这种事可能会降临到我们任何一个人头上。

sentences.en: It's this sort of foreboding.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不祥的预感。

sentences.en: How does that affect the community?
sentences.zh: 这会对社区产生什么影响？

sentences.en: Are there other changes that start to happen?
sentences.zh: 是否还有其他变化开始发生？

sentences.en: So the jobs are real multipliers.
sentences.zh: 这些工作岗位具有真正的乘数效应。

sentences.en: And by that I mean it's not just the GM job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不仅仅是指通用汽车的工作。

sentences.en: It's the suppliers.
sentences.zh: 还有供应商。

sentences.en: It's the parts guys.
sentences.zh: 还有零部件供应商。

sentences.en: It's the window makers.
sentences.zh: 还有窗户制造商。

sentences.en: It's the restaurant nearby that has waitresses and hostesses.
sentences.zh: 还有附近雇有女服务员和迎宾员的餐馆。

sentences.en: So it has a really big effect when these things start happening.
sentences.zh: 因此，当这些事情发生时，会产生非常巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And what happens in large parts of Northeast Ohio and in Ohio more generally, there start to be social problems that come along with this economic decline.
sentences.zh: 在俄亥俄州东北部的大片地区以及更广泛的俄亥俄州，随着这种经济衰退，开始伴随出现各种社会问题。

sentences.en: Men don't have jobs or the jobs they have are not paying enough to support a family.
sentences.zh: 男人们没有工作，或者他们拥有的工作赚取的薪水不足以养家糊口。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's this feeling of worthlessness.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，会有一种毫无价值的失落感。

sentences.en: There's an increase in drinking and drugs.
sentences.zh: 酗酒和吸毒现象增加了。

sentences.en: The rise of single parenthood really soars.
sentences.zh: 单亲家庭的数量急剧上升。

sentences.en: So you have really, in a lot of ways, the breakdown of the family that kind of follows like a wave this economic change.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，你确实能看到家庭的解体，这种经济变革就像浪潮一样随之而来。

sentences.en: OK, I'm going to ask you the question that Dave, the union leader, made fun of you for, which is what are the political implications of all of that?
sentences.zh: 好的，我要问你那个让工会领袖戴夫取笑你的问题，那就是这一切到底会带来什么政治影响？

sentences.en: Did the Democrats pay a price?
sentences.zh: 民主党人付出了代价吗？

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Did the Democrats pay a price?
sentences.zh: 民主党人付出了代价吗？

sentences.en: So what ends up happening is these workers see that, at first don't immediately understand it because it's all kind of out of focus and confusing, but later realize, oh, my God,
sentences.zh: 所以最后发生的情况是，这些工人们看到了这一点，起初并没有立刻理解，因为它有点模糊不清、令人困惑，但后来他们意识到，天哪，

sentences.en: that was our own party that basically gave away the farm.
sentences.zh: 原来是我们自己的党基本上把大家出卖了。

sentences.en: Why did they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: There was this sense of betrayal among workers that actually the Democrats, they weren't that different than the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 工人们有一种被背叛的感觉，觉得民主党人实际上和共和党人没两样。

sentences.en: So from that point on, that union vote, it becomes a little less reliable for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，民主党在工会那里的选票就变得没那么稳固了。

sentences.en: And it's not just NAFTA, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这不仅仅是因为北美自由贸易协定（NAFTA）。

sentences.en: Culturally, things are starting to shift.
sentences.zh: 从文化上看，情况开始发生转变。

sentences.en: And the Democratic Party, it starts to feel alien to many blue-collar workers.
sentences.zh: 民主党开始让许多蓝领工人感到陌生。

sentences.en: And by the time 2008 comes around, it's getting dicey.
sentences.zh: 到了2008年的时候，局势变得有些棘手了。

sentences.en: They end up going for Obama, but more because he was a change guy than because he was a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 他们最后还是投给奥巴马，但与其说是因为他是民主党人，不如说是因为他是一个主张变革的人。

sentences.en: The auto workers were happy.
sentences.zh: 汽车工人们很高兴。

sentences.en: He bailed out GM.
sentences.zh: 他拯救了通用汽车。

sentences.en: But by the end of his second term, their lives hadn't really gotten any better.
sentences.zh: 但到了他第二个任期结束时，他们的生活并没有真正变好。

sentences.en: So by 2016, their heads are basically in this place that's, you know, we'll try anything.
sentences.zh: 所以在2016年，他们的想法基本上变成了，你知道的，我们什么都愿意尝试一下。

sentences.en: And for Trumbull County, that was Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 对于特朗布尔县来说，这个人就是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And I'm like, you know what?
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's a wild card.
sentences.zh: 这是一个未知数。

sentences.en: You know, we need something to shake it up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们需要做点改变来打破僵局。

sentences.en: Our country is a business.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家就像一家公司。

sentences.en: He's a businessman.
sentences.zh: 他是个商人。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And I like the fact that, you know, he made crazy attempts like Trump steaks on Trump college.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢这样的事实，你知道，他尝试过一些疯狂的举动，比如特朗普牛排和特朗普大学。

sentences.en: Like, it's crazy, right?
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, looking back at it now, you're like, that's nuts.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，你会觉得这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: But I applaud him for it because at least you're willing to put it out there on the line and try it.
sentences.zh: 但我为他鼓掌，因为至少你敢于破釜沉舟去尝试。

sentences.en: You know, and if it works, then you're the greatest mastermind to live.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果成功了，那你就是活着的伟大智囊。

sentences.en: And if it fails, well, you know, that was crazy anyway.
sentences.zh: 如果失败了，好吧，你知道，反正那也很疯狂。

sentences.en: Okay,
sentences.zh: 好吧，

sentences.en: so I guess it sort of makes sense that a guy like Brian is not necessarily going to blame Trump for this plant shutting down because he voted for Trump because he's a wild card.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得像布莱恩这样的人不一定会因为这家工厂关闭而怪罪特朗普，这某种程度上也说得通，因为他投票给特朗普就是因为他是个变数。

sentences.en: He's not super surprised or necessarily disappointed that this didn't work out because it was a Hail Mary.
sentences.zh: 他并没有感到超级惊讶，也谈不上彻底失望，因为这本来就是孤注一掷的盲目一搏。

sentences.en: And what the hell else was he going to do?
sentences.zh: 他还能他妈的怎么办呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 对，完全没错。

sentences.en: Do you see Democrats and Republicans as different?
sentences.zh: 你觉得民主党和共和党有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: In terms of parties?
sentences.zh: 就政党而言？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: You don't see them?
sentences.zh: 你看不出区别？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: They're just, it's just politics.
sentences.zh: 它们只是，这只是政治。

sentences.en: It's just a political being.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种政治实体。

sentences.en: There's no red or blue in it for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这里面没有什么红色或蓝色。

sentences.en: How are you making sense of all of this, this feeling that people like Brian have that the two parties aren't all that different?
sentences.zh: 你如何理解这一切？也就是像布莱恩这样的人觉得两党其实没什么区别的这种感觉？

sentences.en: I think for someone like Brian, you know, the important thing is that these processes,
sentences.zh: 我认为对于像布莱恩这样的人来说，你知道，最重要的是这些进程，

sentences.en: these have been happening for a long time and they've been wearing away the community where he lives for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这些进程已经持续了很长时间，并且长期以来一直在侵蚀他生活的社区。

sentences.en: So these things, they're just much deeper than, you know, the most recent political slogan or the way that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这些事情，它们要深远得多，远超你所知道的最近的政治口号，或者你知道的，

sentences.en: the Republicans or the Democrats are going to message this year.
sentences.zh: 今年共和党或民主党会发出什么信息。

sentences.en: It's about this sort of fundamental bedrock of our lives.
sentences.zh: 这关乎我们生活的某种根本基石。

sentences.en: It is just has changed.
sentences.zh: 它确实已经变了。

sentences.en: You can't just graduate from high school and go out and get a job and pay your rent.
sentences.zh: 你不能再仅仅从高中毕业，然后出去找份工作就能付得起房租。

sentences.en: It's not enough money.
sentences.zh: 赚的钱根本不够。

sentences.en: That feels like a real betrayal for people.
sentences.zh: 对人们来说，这感觉像是一种真正的背叛。

sentences.en: It's a set of unmet expectations that I think is causing real political change.
sentences.zh: 这是一系列未能兑现的期望，我认为这正在引发真正的政治变革。

sentences.en: Everything we have is disposable.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的一切都是一次性的。

sentences.en: Everything's made cheap and disposable.
sentences.zh: 所有东西都制造得很廉价且是一次性的。

sentences.en: And I think that trickles down into our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为这已经渗透到了我们的日常生活中。

sentences.en: I mean, you see marriage success rates are down.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看结婚成功率下降了。

sentences.en: You know, things are disposable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一切都是一次性的。

sentences.en: Even on a human level.
sentences.zh: 甚至在人性层面也是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, love.
sentences.zh: 我是说，爱情。

sentences.en: I'm an employee.
sentences.zh: 我是一个雇员。

sentences.en: I'm disposable.
sentences.zh: 我是可以被随手丢弃的。

sentences.en: The old timers, you know, my dad's there, my grandfather's there, they fix things.
sentences.zh: 老一辈的人，你知道的，我父亲在那儿，我祖父在那儿，他们会去修东西。

sentences.en: You know, you had toasters that lasted.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以前的烤面包机能用很久。

sentences.en: You have refrigerators that lasted because people would fix them if something happened.
sentences.zh: 以前的冰箱能用很久，因为如果出了问题，人们会去修好它们。

sentences.en: We didn't just throw them away.
sentences.zh: 我们不会直接把它们扔掉。

sentences.en: You have marriages that went 70 years because people would fix them if they were broken.
sentences.zh: 以前的婚姻能维持70年，因为如果婚姻破裂了，人们会去修复它。

sentences.en: You know, you have people that would, people who have went on strike and have died on picket lines for their companies.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以前有些人，他们为了公司甚至会去罢工，在纠察线上献出生命。

sentences.en: You know, am I willing to lay my life online for the company that is willing to send me a piece of paper and tell me what to do with my life?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我愿意为一家随时准备给我发张纸并对我的生活发号施令的公司拼命吗？

sentences.en: No concern for my family or situation?
sentences.zh: 完全不关心我的家庭或处境？

sentences.en: I just think, I just think it's all broken.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，我只是觉得这一切都崩溃了。

sentences.en: It's like you're asking them, who are you going to vote for at the ballot box in 2020?
sentences.zh: 这就好像你在问他们：“你在2020年的选票箱里打算投给谁？”

sentences.en: And they're asking you, how am I going to make a livelihood in the future when the entire foundation of how I thought this was going to go, I can no longer count on that.
sentences.zh: 而他们却在反问你：“当我原本以为会这样发展的人生基础已经全盘崩塌、再也无法指望时，我未来该怎么谋生？”

sentences.en: The rug has been pulled out from under me.
sentences.zh: 我的人生基石已经被生生地抽掉了。

sentences.en: I don't really want to talk about politics.
sentences.zh: 我其实不想谈论政治。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: What would you hope would be different?
sentences.zh: 你希望有什么改变？

sentences.en: If it were me, I would hope that big companies would cease to exist because once you get so big, you forget where you came from.
sentences.zh: 如果由我决定，我希望大公司不复存在，因为一旦你做到了那么大，你就会忘记自己是从哪里起步的。

sentences.en: And the little guys who make it possible for you to have your giant company and your million dollar salaries, they're just a number to you.
sentences.zh: 而那些让你拥有庞大公司和百万年薪的底层小人物，对你来说只是一个数字。

sentences.en: They're replaceable.
sentences.zh: 他们是随时可以被取代的。

sentences.en: And we were reminded of that in the plant all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们在工厂里时刻都被提醒着这一点。

sentences.en: If you didn't like what was going on, quit.
sentences.zh: 如果你对现状有意见，那就滚蛋。

sentences.en: There's a thousand people that would take this job tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天有的是人排着队想进厂干这份工作呢。

sentences.en: On the other hand, I have to ask whether people like Brian, whether the people you spoke to are hearing the candidates this time around,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我不得不问，像布莱恩这样的人，你交谈过的那些人，他们这次有没有听到候选人们的声音，

sentences.en: the 2020 candidates who are speaking directly to some of the issues that he cares so much about.
sentences.zh: 那些2020年的候选人是否直接回应了他如此关心的某些问题？

sentences.en: Are they being heard?
sentences.zh: 他们的声音被听到了吗？

sentences.en: So the short answer is, at this point, not yet.
sentences.zh: 所以简短的回答是，就目前而言，还没有。

sentences.en: But it is a really interesting political time because for the first time in a really long time, a lot of the candidates on the left are questioning some of these basic things.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一个非常有趣的政治时期，因为在很长一段时间里，许多左翼候选人首次开始对其中一些最基本的事情提出质疑。

sentences.en: I mean, the functioning of American capitalism, that is kind of, you know, a topic of conversation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，美式资本主义的运作方式，这已经成了一个，你知道的，热门话题。

sentences.en: You can have all of the growth that you want, and it doesn't mean anything if all of the new income and wealth is going to the top 1 percent.
sentences.zh: 你可以追求你想要的任何经济增长，但如果所有新增的收入和财富都流入了前1%的人手中，那就没有任何意义。

sentences.en: Who is this economy really working for?
sentences.zh: 这个经济体系到底在为谁服务？

sentences.en: It's doing great for giant drug companies.
sentences.zh: 它对大型制药公司来说好得不得了。

sentences.en: It's just not doing great for people who are trying to get a prescription filled.
sentences.zh: 只是对于那些正努力抓药的人来说不太友好。

sentences.en: When capitalism comes into tension with democracy, which is more important to you?
sentences.zh: 当资本主义与民主发生冲突时，对你来说哪个更重要？

sentences.en: I believe democracy is more important.
sentences.zh: 我相信民主更重要。

sentences.en: So I feel very strongly about the need to check the corporate consolidation and let the free market work.
sentences.zh: 所以我坚信有必要遏制企业垄断，并让自由市场发挥作用。

sentences.en: It is interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Brian is in this group of voters.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩就属于这类选民。

sentences.en: The Democrats know they need to win the election.
sentences.zh: 民主党人知道他们需要赢得大选。

sentences.en: He is really coveted.
sentences.zh: 他正是各方极力争取的目标。

sentences.en: These people want to win him over.
sentences.zh: 这些人想要赢得他的支持。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But he's also really skeptical.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也非常怀疑。

sentences.en: And he's really sick of the political class in the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且他真的厌透了美国的政客阶层。

sentences.en: And he's been burned by both sides at this point.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他已经被两党都深深地伤害过了。

sentences.en: He doesn't trust any political leader to help him.
sentences.zh: 他不相信任何政治领袖会来帮他。

sentences.en: And the consequence is a political system that's still disconnected and pretty unaccountable to people like Brian.
sentences.zh: 其结果就是一个政治体制，它依然与民众脱节，对像布莱恩这样的人来说也几乎毫无问责可言。

sentences.en: You know, I think Brian's going to vote.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得布莱恩会去投票。

sentences.en: He's patriotic and he feels this sense of civic duty.
sentences.zh: 他很有爱国主义精神，并且有一种强烈的公民责任感。

sentences.en: But whether he puts any faith in the person he chooses, that's another question.
sentences.zh: 但至于他对自已选出的人是否还抱有任何信心，那是另一回事了。

sentences.en: They're going to have to work really hard to convince him that he should.
sentences.zh: 他们必须付出极大的努力来让他相信他应该这样做。

sentences.en: Sabrina, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: You're welcome, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 不客气，娜塔莉。

sentences.zh: 通用汽车罗斯敦工厂及其工人的命运是FX和Hulu平台《纽约时报》全新电视节目《一周纪实》（The Weekly）周日晚间播出的单集主题。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 发生地震了，枝形吊灯在晃动。

sentences.en: This is the longest one ever.
sentences.zh: 这是持续时间最长的一次。

sentences.en: On Thursday, a major earthquake struck Southern California, starting in a relatively secluded area of the Mojave Desert and shaking structures up to 150 miles away.
sentences.zh: 周四，一场强烈地震袭击了南加州，震源始于莫哈韦沙漠一个相对偏僻的地区，连150英里外的建筑物都感到了震动。

sentences.en: The quake registered 6.4 on the Richter scale and set off 87 aftershocks, making it the most powerful tremor to hit the region in two decades.
sentences.zh: 此次地震震级为里氏6.4级，并引发了87次余震，使其成为该地区二十年来遭遇的最强烈震动。

sentences.en: As of Thursday night, no deaths were reported, but there was damage to homes, roads and water means across the region.
sentences.zh: 截至周四晚间，暂无人员伤亡报告，但该地区的住宅、道路和水管均受到损坏。

sentences.en: And 243 years ago, our founding fathers pledged their lives, their fortunes and their sacred honor to declare independence and defend our God-given rights.
sentences.zh: 243年前，我们的建国先辈们誓以生命、财富和神圣的荣誉来宣布独立并捍卫上帝赋予我们的权利。

sentences.en: President Trump presided over a sprawling and controversial celebration of American independence, delivering a speech in front of the Lincoln Memorial,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统主持了一场规模宏大且备受争议的美国独立日庆典，他在林肯纪念堂前发表了演讲，

sentences.en: surrounded by armored vehicles, including tanks, and with military jets flying overhead.
sentences.zh: 周围环绕着包括坦克在内的装甲车，头顶还有军用喷气式飞机呼啸而过。

sentences.en: The presidential rally drew thousands of supporters, as well as hundreds of protesters.
sentences.zh: 这场总统集会吸引了数千名支持者，同时也引来了数百名抗议者。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎进了一群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
